page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is provisioned with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the E16s_v7 demonstrates balanced performance across compute and memory subsystems. Its single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU performance falls within the average range, as does its PassMark CPU score of 26,408.67. However, it exhibits strong single-threaded gzip compression at 35.26 GB/sec and strong text generation speeds of 319.32 tokens/sec for small 135M language models. Memory bandwidth is measured at 133.34 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 68.36 GB/sec for large block write operations. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider for I/O-heavy workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16s_v7 provides a high density of memory relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is well-suited for relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers like Redis (achieving 26.17 million operations/sec in SET benchmarks), enterprise applications, and moderate data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E16s_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an 8-core Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. It delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The architecture features a 480 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. While it lacks local storage and GPUs, it is Premium Storage capable. Benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU performance alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and small-model LLM text generation. The instance is optimized for memory-intensive workloads such as databases, in-memory caches, and enterprise applications requiring high memory density without excessive compute overhead.
